name: UC Riverside soft bidirectional SMA actu
full_name: UC Riverside soft bidirectional SMA actuator catheter: silicone body with a U-shaped SMA wire and a pre-stretched elastic band on a braid-reinforced shaft
group: University of California Riverside, Dept. of Mechanical Engineering (J. Sheng, K. Oda, P. AfshariNejad, K. Lee, A. Akbari) and Dept. of Materials Science and Engineering (V. Manian) (manian2025_soft p. 1 footnote)
versions: single version (manian2025_soft, IEEE RA-L 10(10):10274-10281, 2025); builds on the group's earlier SMA model (ref. [18] in the paper, not read)
target_anatomy: cardiovascular catheterization, 'diagnostic evaluation and therapeutic interventions' with stent delivery and angioplasty named (Sec. I); demonstrated in a 3D-printed half-open type 1 aortic arch phantom: left subclavian, left common carotid and brachiocephalic arteries (Sec. VI, Fig. 7)
devices_driven: own steerable catheter robot: soft SMA actuator (Dragon Skin 10 silicone, U-shaped SMA wire 0.5 mm x 130 mm, elastic band 16 mm stretched to 36 mm) joined by heat shrink to a braid-reinforced tube shaft (Duke Extrusion); one device (Sec. II-A, VI)
n_dof_detail: 1 active bending DOF (bidirectional, one plane); insertion and rotation by hand at the base (Sec. VI, Fig. 1)
translation_detail: tendon/tip-actuation: Joule heating of the SMA wire under micro-temperature-sensor feedback bends the tip between positive and negative curvature (Sec. II-A, V-A); insertion by hand ('translating and rotating the base of the robot', Sec. VI)
rotation_detail: by hand at the base of the shaft (Sec. VI)
device_range: actuator 'sub-5 mm envelope', diagonal size to be cut to 3 mm in future work (Sec. VII); shaft diameter and length N.R.; Table I geometry not in the text layer
force_sensing: none (micro temperature sensors on the actuator; load cell only for the elastic-band characterisation, Sec. IV-A)
haptics_leader: none; the user sets the SMA temperature by hand and watches the phantom directly (Sec. VI)
imaging_compat: optical: direct visual feedback of the phantom (Sec. VI); fluoroscopy and MRI N.R.
sterility: N.R.; the Discussion plans for single-use surgical robots with finite motion cycles, likely < 100 (Sec. VII)
validation_detail: bench: quasi-static bending angle vs SMA temperature, 3 cycles (Sec. V-D, Fig. 6); 150 heating-cooling cycles, 2.4 A for 11 s, 35 s cooling (Sec. V-B, Fig. 5b); surface temperature in 37 C water (Sec. V-C); phantom: three demonstrations, one per artery, each within 30 s (Sec. VI, Fig. 7); no repeat counts or success rates
key_numbers: bending -70 to +71 deg, model R2 0.995, RMSE 4.3 deg (martensite to austenite) and 2.0 deg (reverse) (Sec. V-D; Fig. 6 caption prints 4.2 deg); max difference between the three cycles 3.7 and 3.1 deg; range falls over the first 60 cycles, to -59.7 / +59.4 deg at 100 cycles (Sec. V-B); highest surface temperature about 46 C at SMA 70 C (Sec. V-C); demo bends of about -36 deg in 2 s (SMA at 51 C) and about -47 deg in 2.2 s (54 C) (Sec. VI)
sim_model: quasi-static model coupling the SMA constitutive relation (Liang-Rogers) with the elastic-band mechanics; no vessel simulation (manian2025_soft Sec. III, V-D)

sources.title: Soft Bidirectional Shape Memory Alloy Actuators for Robotic Catheters

notes: REV4 2026-11-23: included after the full assessment of the 19 candidates (REV4_19_candidates.md §7). Shown as an open draftnote in the supplement (supplement_05_06.tex, 'manian2025_soft is still not a row'). Insertion and rotation are manual, so this is a steerable-tip device, not a drive. The abstract's 'about 120 deg' is the -70 to +71 deg range of Sec. V-D.
